newsitem.title: MALDIVES: South Asian states said not deterred by sub-group.
newsitem.headline: South Asian states said not deterred by sub-group.

text.p: South Asian countries preparing for a summit in Male will not allow a proposed sub-regional grouping to affect their association, Maldivian Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Solah Shihab said on Friday.
He said the seven-nation South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC) remained committed to the organisation's success.

"It is not an issue we would ignore," Shihab told a news conference. "But all seven member states are very firmly committed to SAARC. They would not want any divisions that would affect SAARC's unity."

He was refering to a new trade group for choser economic co-coperation proposed by Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Bhutan last month because SAARC itself has been largely ineffective owing to rivalry between India and Pakistan.
The new Growth Quadrangle group was orignally planned as a SAARC sub-group but developed separately after oppositon from Pakistan, which said it would undermine SAARC.
SAARC, launched in 1985, groups India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, the Maldives and Bhutan.
"Whatever is done on a bilateral or quadrangular basis should not affect the progress of SAARC," Shihab said. "We have a very clear understanding on that. We would not let it in any way harm SAARC."
He said the meeting of heads of state in the Maldives would look for ways to pursue sub-regional co-operation in an open manner so that there would be no misunderstanding among members.
Shihab acknowledged that SAARC's progress had been slow but said the summit in Male on May 12-14 would try to find ways of streamlining its work to make the organisation more efficient.
The organisation plans to form a regional free-trade zone by the year 2005.
Two rounds of talks under the South Asian Preferential Trade Agreement signed in 1995 have already been held with member states exchanging tariff concessions on 2,459 items.
Foreign ministers of the member states will meet on Saturday to discuss the reports of the group's working committees and to work on the final summit declaration, Shihab said.
